literature.headline_zh: 尼帕病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期尼帕病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 最终的CNB-LFIA在15分钟内即可得出结果,并实现了对重组NiV NP的分析检测限为1 ng/mL。 [10.1080/22221751.2026.2716499]

我们的结果显示,IFNAR KO小鼠对尼帕病毒孟加拉国株的腹腔感染表现出易感性,尽管程度不如尼帕病毒马来西亚株,且在60%的感染小鼠中出现脑炎和肺综合征,病毒传播至不同器官并导致死亡。两种病毒株通过鼻腔途径给药均导致亚临床感染,病毒在脑和肺中复制,并产生病毒特异性中和抗体。最后,每种病毒株和特定感染途径均与不同的组织病理学表现和病毒嗜性相关。 [10.1371/journal.pntd.0013894]
NV1和NV3诱导了针对NiV假病毒的强效结合抗体和强中和活性。NV2虽缺乏中和活性,但诱导了优越的Th1偏向性细胞免疫,并伴有广泛的T细胞克隆增殖。 [10.3390/vaccines14080718]
MSA 分析表明,尼帕病毒 及其相关病毒的 RdRp 使用 -LA/VG- 作为模板结合对,一个不变的 K 作为质子抽取剂,启动催化反应,并且一个位于催化 K 前第 4 位的不变 R 作为核苷酸识别器,所有这些都高度或完全保守。此外,催化镁结合位点也被发现完全保守,由两个不变的天冬氨酸含有的模体 -GDN- 和 -TDL- 组成。 [10.30574/wjarr.2026.31.2.2181]
目前 NiV 的管理在很大程度上仍然是支持性的,没有获得许可的 抗病毒药物 或 疫苗,因此强调需要采取有效的医疗对策。 [10.7860/jcdr/2026/87496.24264]
literature.trend_or_risk_zh: 本期研究方向以入选文献实际覆盖的临床、流行病学、宿主生态、诊断或分子监测主题为准。
literature.lead_en: This reporting window highlights the following research developments.
key_findings_en: The finalized CNB-LFIA produced results within 15 min and achieved an analytical limit of detection of 1 ng/mL for recombinant NiV NP. [10.1080/22221751.2026.2716499]

Our results show that IFNAR KO mice are susceptible to NiV-Ban infection via intraperitoneal route, although to a lesser extent than NiV-Mal, and develop encephalitis and pulmonary syndrome with viral propagation to different organs and lethal outcome in 60% of infected animals. [10.1371/journal.pntd.0013894]

The results revealed a total of 12 highly antigenic and non-allergenic epitopes comprising of 4 T-cell, 4 B-cell, and 4 HTL demonstrating a high population coverage (> 90%) and 100% conservancy across the three studied strains. [10.1007/s00210-026-05738-3]

NV1 and NV3 induced potent binding antibodies and strong neutralizing activity against NiV pseudoviruses. NV2 lacked neutralizing activity but induced superior Th1-biased cellular immunity, accompanied by extensive T-cell clonal proliferation. [10.3390/vaccines14080718]

The MSA analysis revealed that the RdRp of Nipah virus and related viruses uses an -LA/VG- as the template-binding pair, an invariant K as the proton abstractor initiating catalysis, and an invariant R at -4 from the catalytic K as the nucleotide discriminator, all of which are highly or completely conserved. [10.30574/wjarr.2026.31.2.2181]

papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is known to be an emerging zoonotic pathogen of the Paramyxoviridae family, which was first identified in 1998, and is also associated with high morbidity and mortality due to severe encephalitis and respiratory illness. Transmission occurs through direct contact with infected animals, contaminated food, and human-to-human transmission , thereby further highlighting its epidemic potential. Despite significant advances in understanding its virology, pathogenesis, as well as clinical manifestations, NiV outbreaks continue to pose substantial public health challenges, usually in endemic regions. Current management of NiV remains largely supportive with no licensed antivirals or vaccines available, thus emphasising the need for effective medical countermeasures. Recent therapeutic developments must focus on monoclonal antibodies and antiviral agents, including Remdesivir, which have shown promising efficacy in preclinical studies. Vaccine candidates, including recombinant protein, viral vector, and mRNA-based platforms, are being examined in their early phases of clinical evaluation, showing potential for robust protection of immunity. Future research priorities must include the development of rapid point-of-care diagnosis, strengthening genomic surveillance while also implementing One Health approaches integrating human, animal and environmental data for the prevention of spillover events. Refining animal models and elucidating immune correlates of protection are very important aspects for translating preclinical successes into adequately licensed interventions for management approaches for NiV. Collaborative international frameworks as well as structured R&D roadmaps are critical options for the acceleration of vaccine and therapeutic development, thereby further ensuring rapid deployment during outbreaks. This narrative review article highlights current knowledge on the epidemiology of NiV, pathogenesis, clinical management, as well as emerging preventive-therapeutic strategies while also identifying critical research gaps. It underscores the need for a proactive, integrated approach which combines medical, public health and scientific efforts for the mitigation of the threat of NiV globally.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review provides an overview of Nipah virus (NiV) infection, focusing on its clinical spectrum, pathogenesis, and the development of preventive and therapeutic strategies. NiV, a zoonotic pathogen of the Paramyxoviridae family, is associated with severe encephalitis and respiratory illness, with high morbidity and mortality. Transmission occurs through direct contact with infected animals, contaminated food, and human-to-human routes, highlighting its epidemic potential. Despite advances in understanding its virology and pathogenesis, NiV outbreaks continue to pose significant public health challenges. Current management is supportive, with no licensed antivirals or vaccines available, underscoring the need for effective medical countermeasures. Recent therapeutic developments, including monoclonal antibodies and antiviral agents like Remdesivir, show promise in preclinical studies. Vaccine candidates, such as recombinant protein, viral vector, and mRNA-based platforms, are in early clinical evaluation. The review highlights the importance of refining animal models and understanding immune correlates of protection to translate preclinical findings into licensed interventions. It also stresses the need for rapid point-of-care diagnosis, genomic surveillance, and One Health approaches to prevent spillover events. Collaborative international frameworks and structured R&D roadmaps are critical for accelerating vaccine and therapeutic development. The review identifies critical research gaps and underscores the necessity of a proactive, integrated approach combining medical, public health, and scientific efforts to mitigate the global threat of NiV.

papers.abstract_zh: 尼帕病毒 (NiV) 已知是副粘病毒科的一种新出现的人畜共患病原体,于 1998 年首次发现,并且由于严重的 脑炎 和呼吸道疾病,也与高发病率和 死亡率 相关。传播通过直接接触受感染的动物、受污染的食物以及人与人之间的传播发生,从而进一步凸显了其流行潜力。尽管在了解其病毒学、发病机制 以及临床表现方面取得了重大进展,但 NiV 暴发 仍然对公共卫生构成重大挑战,通常是在流行地区。目前 NiV 的管理在很大程度上仍然是支持性的,没有获得许可的 抗病毒药物 或 疫苗,因此强调需要采取有效的医疗对策。最近的治疗发展必须集中在单克隆抗体和 抗病毒药物 药物上,包括瑞德西韦,它们在临床前研究中显示出有希望的疗效。疫苗 候选药物,包括重组蛋白、病毒 媒介 和基于 mRNA 的平台,正在临床评估的早期阶段进行检查,显示出强大的免疫保护潜力。未来的研究重点必须包括开发快速护理点 诊断、加强 基因组监测,同时实施整合人类、动物和环境数据的“同一个健康”方法,以预防 跨物种溢出 事件。完善动物模型和阐明保护的免疫相关性是将临床前成功转化为获得充分许可的 NiV 管理方法干预措施的非常重要的方面。国际协作框架以及结构化研发路线图是加速 疫苗 和治疗开发的关键选择,从而进一步确保 暴发 期间的快速部署。这篇叙述性综述文章重点介绍了 NiV 的 流行病学、发病机制、临床管理以及新兴预防治疗策略的当前知识,同时还确定了关键的研究差距。它强调需要采取积极主动的综合方法,将医疗、公共卫生和科学努力结合起来,以减轻全球新病毒的威胁。

papers.title: Nipah virus Malaysia and Bangladesh strain-induced pathogenesis in mice lacking type I interferon receptor signaling
papers.abstract: Abstract Nipah virus (NiV) is a zoonotic highly pathogenic Paramyxovirus inducing lethal outbreaks of encephalitis and severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS) with an average case-fatality rate of 75%. Two viral strains, NiV-Malaysia (NiV-Mal) and NiV-Bangladesh (NiV-Ban), associated to distinct geographical distribution, route of transmission, symptoms and lethality have been described. Due to the permanent threat of these emerging infections and the lack of approved therapeutics, it is crucial to improve our understanding regarding NiV-associated pathogenesis. Mice represent a small and accessible animal model, provided with numerous biological tools for the functional assessment of different genes related to antiviral response. Here, we analyze the susceptibility of mice deficient for type I interferon receptor (IFNAR KO) to infection with either NiV-Mal or NiV-Ban through intraperitoneal or intranasal routes. Our results show that IFNAR KO mice are susceptible to NiV-Ban infection via intraperitoneal route, although to a lesser extent than NiV-Mal, and develop encephalitis and pulmonary syndrome with viral propagation to different organs and lethal outcome in 60% of infected animals. In addition, intranasal administration of both viral strains led to a subclinical infection with viral replication in brain and lungs and production of virus-specific neutralizing antibodies. These results indicate IFNAR KO mice as a small animal model permitting comparative studies of the immunopathogenesis perpetrated by both NiV-Mal and NiV-Ban infections. Author summary Availability of small animal models represents a major issue to characterize virus-associated pathogenesis to further implement therapeutic strategies. Previous studies performed with NiV-Mal and NiV-Ban strains in wild-type (WT) mice did not indicate signs of NiV disease. However, when challenged with NiV-Mal, IFNAR KO mice suffered fatal outcomes, thus providing useful information on viral immunopathogenesis. Surprisingly, while being the more frequently re-emerging virus strain, no infection studies with NiV-Ban have been performed in IFNAR KO mice so far. Here, we sought comparing pathogenesis after NiV-Mal- and NiV-Ban-infection following IP and IN inoculations in IFNAR KO mice. Indeed, our results highlighted that contrary to fatal IP challenge, IN inoculation lead to a subclinical infection with both NiV strains. Moreover, we determined that NiV-Mal is more pathogenic than NiV-Ban following IP infection. Finally, distinct histopathological manifestations and tropism were associated with each viral strain and specific route of infection. Overall, our study implies that IFNAR KO mice represent a useful animal model to study strain-specific NiV pathophysiology.

papers.source_body_en: Abstract Nipah virus (NiV) is a zoonotic highly pathogenic Paramyxovirus inducing lethal outbreaks of encephalitis and severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS) with an average case-fatality rate of 75%. Two viral strains, NiV-Malaysia (NiV-Mal) and NiV-Bangladesh (NiV-Ban), associated to distinct geographical distribution, route of transmission, symptoms and lethality have been described. Due to the permanent threat of these emerging infections and the lack of approved therapeutics, it is crucial to improve our understanding regarding NiV-associated pathogenesis. Mice represent a small and accessible animal model, provided with numerous biological tools for the functional assessment of different genes related to antiviral response. Here, we analyze the susceptibility of mice deficient for type I interferon receptor (IFNAR KO) to infection with either NiV-Mal or NiV-Ban through intraperitoneal or intranasal routes. Our results show that IFNAR KO mice are susceptible to NiV-Ban infection via intraperitoneal route, although to a lesser extent than NiV-Mal, and develop encephalitis and pulmonary syndrome with viral propagation to different organs and lethal outcome in 60% of infected animals. In addition, intranasal administration of both viral strains led to a subclinical infection with viral replication in brain and lungs and production of virus-specific neutralizing antibodies. These results indicate IFNAR KO mice as a small animal model permitting comparative studies of the immunopathogenesis perpetrated by both NiV-Mal and NiV-Ban infections. Author summary Availability of small animal models represents a major issue to characterize virus-associated pathogenesis to further implement therapeutic strategies. Previous studies performed with NiV-Mal and NiV-Ban strains in wild-type (WT) mice did not indicate signs of NiV disease. However, when challenged with NiV-Mal, IFNAR KO mice suffered fatal outcomes, thus providing useful information on viral immunopathogenesis. Surprisingly, while being the more frequently re-emerging virus strain, no infection studies with NiV-Ban have been performed in IFNAR KO mice so far. Here, we sought comparing pathogenesis after NiV-Mal- and NiV-Ban-infection following IP and IN inoculations in IFNAR KO mice. Indeed, our results highlighted that contrary to fatal IP challenge, IN inoculation lead to a subclinical infection with both NiV strains. Moreover, we determined that NiV-Mal is more pathogenic than NiV-Ban following IP infection. Finally, distinct histopathological manifestations and tropism were associated with each viral strain and specific route of infection. Overall, our study implies that IFNAR KO mice represent a useful animal model to study strain-specific NiV pathophysiology.

papers.title: Proteome conserved multi-epitope-based vaccine construct against Nipah virus
papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly pathogenic virus with no available FDA-approved medication. Herein, immunoinformatic-based approaches may serve as a crucial method for rapid development of vaccine targeting the emerging strains of the NiV. The study utilizes immunoinformatic-based computational methodology to design multi-epitope subunit vaccine by deciphering highly conserved antigenic epitopes across NiV strains. The NiV whole proteome (UP000002330) was subjected to shortlist immune epitopes based on high antigenic scores, non-allergenic status, broad HLA population coverage, and 100% conservancy across three different demographic NiV strains. The obtained primary sequence of the MEVC construct was then 3D modelled using AlphaFold2 server and validated through PROSA web analysis. The interaction profile of the proposed multi-epitope-based vaccine construct and immune receptor TLR3 was also explored with molecular docking and normal mode analysis. The conformational stability of the complex was confirmed through a triplicate of 200-ns molecular dynamics simulation. Finally, in silico cloning construct and immune simulation data for the proposed vaccine were also depicted. The results revealed a total of 12 highly antigenic and non-allergenic epitopes comprising of 4 T-cell, 4 B-cell, and 4 HTL demonstrating a high population coverage (> 90%) and 100% conservancy across the three studied strains. The 3D validated structure of the proposed vaccine through molecular docking studies suggested a stronger total binding free energy of - 62.83 (kcal/mol) and formation of 10 hydrogen bonds, 2 salt bridges, and 10 hydrophobic interactions with human TLR3 structure. The NMA analysis showed minimal fluctuations of the complex and an eigenvalue of 3.96 × 10 -6 . Molecular dynamics simulations exhibited stable complexes with RMSD and RMSF values ranging from 0 to 20. The optimal vaccine sequence was computationally cloned into the pET-28a (+) vector and immune simulation depicted an organized immune response with elevated levels of IgG1 and IgG2, activated T- and B-cell populations, and potential memory cell development. The study provides baseline data, and a 3D validated design of a novel MEVC-NIPAH vaccine through multi-scale computational analysis. Further experimental validations will be required to clarify the protective efficacy and potential translation of the proposed vaccine into clinical settings.

analysis.summary_en: This study presents a computational approach to design a multi-epitope-based vaccine (MEVC-NIPAH) against Nipah virus (NiV), a highly pathogenic virus with no FDA-approved treatment. The vaccine construct was developed by identifying conserved antigenic epitopes across three NiV strains, validated through 3D modeling and molecular docking, and demonstrated stable interactions with TLR3. The results showed 12 epitopes with high population coverage and 100% conservancy, along with a strong binding free energy and multiple interaction types. The study provides a baseline for vaccine design but emphasizes the need for further experimental validation to assess its protective efficacy and clinical potential. The findings are significant for developing surveillance and prevention strategies against NiV, but the evidence strength is moderate due to the absence of empirical testing.

papers.title_zh: 基于蛋白质组保守多表位的疫苗构建物对抗尼帕病毒病毒
papers.source_body_en: Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly pathogenic virus with no available FDA-approved medication. Herein, immunoinformatic-based approaches may serve as a crucial method for rapid development of vaccine targeting the emerging strains of the NiV. The study utilizes immunoinformatic-based computational methodology to design multi-epitope subunit vaccine by deciphering highly conserved antigenic epitopes across NiV strains. The NiV whole proteome (UP000002330) was subjected to shortlist immune epitopes based on high antigenic scores, non-allergenic status, broad HLA population coverage, and 100% conservancy across three different demographic NiV strains. The obtained primary sequence of the MEVC construct was then 3D modelled using AlphaFold2 server and validated through PROSA web analysis. The interaction profile of the proposed multi-epitope-based vaccine construct and immune receptor TLR3 was also explored with molecular docking and normal mode analysis. The conformational stability of the complex was confirmed through a triplicate of 200-ns molecular dynamics simulation. Finally, in silico cloning construct and immune simulation data for the proposed vaccine were also depicted. The results revealed a total of 12 highly antigenic and non-allergenic epitopes comprising of 4 T-cell, 4 B-cell, and 4 HTL demonstrating a high population coverage (> 90%) and 100% conservancy across the three studied strains. The 3D validated structure of the proposed vaccine through molecular docking studies suggested a stronger total binding free energy of - 62.83 (kcal/mol) and formation of 10 hydrogen bonds, 2 salt bridges, and 10 hydrophobic interactions with human TLR3 structure. The NMA analysis showed minimal fluctuations of the complex and an eigenvalue of 3.96 × 10 -6 . Molecular dynamics simulations exhibited stable complexes with RMSD and RMSF values ranging from 0 to 20. The optimal vaccine sequence was computationally cloned into the pET-28a (+) vector and immune simulation depicted an organized immune response with elevated levels of IgG1 and IgG2, activated T- and B-cell populations, and potential memory cell development. The study provides baseline data, and a 3D validated design of a novel MEVC-NIPAH vaccine through multi-scale computational analysis. Further experimental validations will be required to clarify the protective efficacy and potential translation of the proposed vaccine into clinical settings.

papers.title: A rapid detection of Nipah virus nucleocapsid antigen in inactivated viral cultures
papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly lethal zoonotic henipavirus that causes severe respiratory disease and encephalitis and remains a priority pathogen for outbreak preparedness. Timely diagnosis is essential for containment, yet nucleic acid-based testing is often impractical in outbreak-prone, resource-limited settings. Here, we report the development of a rapid antigen test for NiV based on a cellulose nanobead (CNB)-enhanced lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA) targeting the viral nucleocapsid protein (NP). Anti-NiV NP antibodies were isolated from human synthetic phage-display libraries (scFv and Fab) by iterative bio-panning, reformatted as full-length IgGs, and screened using ELISA and immunofluorescence assays. Four lead antibodies were advanced to a sandwich-pairing matrix, which identified an optimized capture-detection configuration (mAb #5 as capture; mAb #2 as detection). Bio-layer interferometry confirmed nanomolar binding affinities for the selected antibodies (KD = 39.50 nM for mAb #5; KD = 26.36 nM for mAb #2). The finalized CNB-LFIA produced results within 15 min and achieved an analytical limit of detection of 1 ng/mL for recombinant NiV NP. The assay observed no cross-reactivity with SARS-CoV-2, SARS-CoV, MERS-CoV, or influenza A, whereas weak cross-reactivity for measles virus NP was observed only at a high antigen concentration (2 μg/mL). Using γ-irradiated cultured NiV quantified by RT-ddPCR, the LFIA detected viral load down to 4.1 × 107 copies/mL (4.1 × 106 copies/reaction) by a portable reader and 8.3 × 107 copies/mL (8.3 × 106 copies/reaction) by the naked eye. Collectively, this CNB-LFIA provides rapid, equipment-free NiV detection, supporting its potential utility for point-of-care diagnosis in resource-limited settings.

papers.title_zh: 一种快速检测尼帕病毒核衣壳抗原的方法
papers.source_body_en: Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly lethal zoonotic henipavirus that causes severe respiratory disease and encephalitis and remains a priority pathogen for outbreak preparedness. Timely diagnosis is essential for containment, yet nucleic acid-based testing is often impractical in outbreak-prone, resource-limited settings. Here, we report the development of a rapid antigen test for NiV based on a cellulose nanobead (CNB)-enhanced lateral flow immunoassay (LFIA) targeting the viral nucleocapsid protein (NP). Anti-NiV NP antibodies were isolated from human synthetic phage-display libraries (scFv and Fab) by iterative bio-panning, reformatted as full-length IgGs, and screened using ELISA and immunofluorescence assays. Four lead antibodies were advanced to a sandwich-pairing matrix, which identified an optimized capture-detection configuration (mAb #5 as capture; mAb #2 as detection). Bio-layer interferometry confirmed nanomolar binding affinities for the selected antibodies (KD = 39.50 nM for mAb #5; KD = 26.36 nM for mAb #2). The finalized CNB-LFIA produced results within 15 min and achieved an analytical limit of detection of 1 ng/mL for recombinant NiV NP. The assay observed no cross-reactivity with SARS-CoV-2, SARS-CoV, MERS-CoV, or influenza A, whereas weak cross-reactivity for measles virus NP was observed only at a high antigen concentration (2 μg/mL). Using γ-irradiated cultured NiV quantified by RT-ddPCR, the LFIA detected viral load down to 4.1 × 107 copies/mL (4.1 × 106 copies/reaction) by a portable reader and 8.3 × 107 copies/mL (8.3 × 106 copies/reaction) by the naked eye. Collectively, this CNB-LFIA provides rapid, equipment-free NiV detection, supporting its potential utility for point-of-care diagnosis in resource-limited settings.

papers.title: Epitope-Based Nipah Virus G and F Head-to-Head Dimer mRNA Vaccines Exhibit Distinct Immunogenicity and Immune Profiles
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives: Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly pathogenic zoonotic agent that causes fatal respiratory and neurological diseases, for which no approved vaccines are currently available. To address this unmet need, we developed and evaluated novel mRNA-LNP vaccine candidates. These vaccines employ an epitope- and structure–guided “immune-focusing” strategy, aiming to maximize the exposure of critical neutralizing epitopes on the viral attachment (G) and fusion (F) glycoproteins. Methods: Head-to-head dimeric antigens (2Gs and 2Fs) were engineered by removing subdominant stalk regions and tandemly duplicating epitope-rich globular head domains. Three LNP-encapsulated candidates-NV1 (encoding 2Gs), NV2 (encoding 2Fs), and NV3 (a 1:1 mixture of NV1 and NV2)-were evaluated in BALB/c mice and Syrian hamsters to systematically assess humoral responses, cytokine secretion, BCR/TCR repertoires, and systemic safety. Results: NV1 and NV3 induced potent binding antibodies and strong neutralizing activity against NiV pseudoviruses. Meanwhile, although NV2 lacked neutralizing activity, it induced superior Th1-biased cellular immunity, accompanied by extensive T-cell clonal proliferation. The study aimed to develop and evaluate novel vaccine strategies to address this unmet need.

analysis.summary_en: This study aimed to develop and evaluate novel mRNA-LNP vaccines targeting Nipah virus (NiV) to address the lack of approved vaccines for this highly pathogenic zoonotic agent. The vaccines were designed using an epitope- and structure-guided strategy, with NV1 encoding dimeric G glycoproteins, NV2 encoding dimeric F glycoproteins, and NV3 combining both. The study assessed immunogenicity in BALB/c mice and Syrian hamsters, revealing that NV1 and NV3 induced strong neutralizing antibodies, while NV2 promoted superior Th1-biased cellular immunity. BCR/TCR sequencing highlighted unique immune responses corresponding to the vaccine designs. Preliminary safety assessments showed no toxicity to vital organs, and immune mobilization was confirmed through active germinal center formation. The results suggest that an epitope-centered dimer design can shape distinct immune responses, with NV3 offering a balanced strategy for vaccine development. However, the study is limited to animal models, and the evidence is moderate due to the absence of human trials.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 尼帕病毒(尼帕病毒,NiV)是一种高致病性人兽共患病原体,可引发致命的呼吸系统和神经系统疾病,目前尚无获批的疫苗(疫苗)。本研究旨在开发并评估新型疫苗策略以满足这一未被满足的需求。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 三种LNP包裹的疫苗候选物——NV1(编码2Gs)、NV2(编码2Fs)和NV3(NV1与NV2的1:1混合物)——在BALB/c小鼠和叙利亚仓鼠中进行评估,以系统性评估体液免疫应答、细胞因子分泌、BCR/TCR库以及全身安全性。
elements_zh.methods: 通过移除次要茎区并串联重复富含表位的球状头部结构域,构建了头对头二聚体抗原(2Gs和2Fs)。采用BCR/TCR测序以揭示与疫苗不同免疫原性特征相一致的独特适应性免疫特征。
elements_zh.main_results: NV1和NV3诱导了针对NiV假病毒的强效结合抗体和强中和活性。NV2虽缺乏中和活性,但诱导了优越的Th1偏向性细胞免疫,并伴有广泛的T细胞克隆增殖。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 以表位为中心的二聚体设计有效塑造了适应性免疫系统的独特防御机制。NV3提供了一种平衡且协同的策略,结合了强效的体液和细胞免疫防御。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果为开发尼帕病毒(NiV)疫苗提供了极具前景的平台,并为疫苗设计提供了见解,有望为未来的监测(诊断)、诊断(治疗)和预防策略提供参考。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究仅限于动物模型,结果可能无法完全转化为人类免疫应答。证据强度为中等,因研究结果基于小鼠和仓鼠的免疫原性和免疫特征评估。

papers.title: The Role of the Medical Laboratory in Identifying 'Super-Spreaders': Correlation Between Viral Load Kinetics and Human-to-Human Infectivity.
papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a high-consequence zoonotic henipavirus characterised by severe encephalitis and respiratory distress, driving recurrent outbreaks with case fatality rates between 40% and 75% in India and Bangladesh. Within these outbreaks, 'super-spreading' dynamics play a critical role, where a small subset of individuals contributes to a disproportionately large share of secondary infections. To evaluate the relationship between human infectivity and viral load kinetics in Nipah virus infection and to define the role of the medical laboratory in identifying potential super-spreaders, a narrative review was conducted by executing a systematic search across PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect for peer-reviewed literature published from 1998 to 2025. The qualitative synthesis demonstrated that NiV infectivity is highly dependent on specimen matrix efficiency and anatomical shedding patterns. Respiratory specimens yield the highest viral RNA copy numbers during the acute symptomatic phase, correlating strongly with active droplet transmission. Persistent real-time RT-PCR Cycle Threshold values below 25 (Ct < 25) in respiratory samples serve as an indirect laboratory indicator of high-risk shedders and should be interpreted alongside clinical and epidemiological findings. However, a comprehensive analysis indicates that super-spreading is inherently multifactorial. Early identification via frontline molecular diagnostics remains the cornerstone of breaking NiV transmission chains. Although a standalone viral load threshold is insufficient to predict a spreading event on its own, the medical laboratory provides an essential risk profile by combining longitudinal Ct kinetics with clinical and exposure data. Strengthening regional laboratory infrastructure and deploying standardized point-of-care molecular assays in endemic, resource-limited areas are urgent public health priorities.

To evaluate the relationship between human infectivity and viral load kinetics in Nipah virus infection and to define the role of the medical laboratory in identifying potential super-spreaders, a narrative review was conducted by executing a systematic search across PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect for peer-reviewed literature published from 1998 to 2025. The qualitative synthesis demonstrated that NiV infectivity is highly dependent on specimen matrix efficiency and anatomical shedding patterns. Respiratory specimens yield the highest viral RNA copy numbers during the acute symptomatic phase, correlating strongly with active droplet transmission. Persistent real-time RT-PCR Cycle Threshold values below 25 (Ct < 25) in respiratory samples serve as an indirect laboratory indicator of high-risk shedders and should be interpreted alongside clinical and epidemiological findings. However, a comprehensive analysis indicates that super-spreading is inherently multifactorial. Early identification via frontline molecular diagnostics remains the cornerstone of breaking NiV transmission chains. Although a standalone viral load threshold is insufficient to predict a spreading event on its own, the medical laboratory provides an essential risk profile by combining longitudinal Ct kinetics with clinical and exposure data. Strengthening regional laboratory infrastructure and deploying standardized point-of-care molecular assays in endemic, resource-limited areas are urgent public health priorities.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于尼帕病毒(NiV)感染与疾病,重点探讨病毒载量动态与人际传播感染性之间的关联。核心问题是医学实验室如何通过病毒载量分析识别潜在超级传播者,以及其对尼帕病毒防控的意义。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述采用叙事综述方法,系统检索了1998年至2025年间在PubMed、Scopus及ScienceDirect发表的同行评审文献。纳入研究涵盖尼帕病毒传播性、病毒载量动态及分子诊断在识别超级传播者中的作用。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 定性综合分析表明,尼帕病毒感染性高度依赖于标本基质效率和解剖学排毒模式。急性症状期呼吸道标本中病毒RNA拷贝数最高,与活跃的飞沫传播高度相关。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 全面分析显示,超级传播本质上是多因素的,单一因素(包括病毒载量)无法独立预测传播事件。综述强调需将纵向Ct动态与临床和流行病学数据整合,以实现准确的风险分层。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 加强区域实验室基础设施建设,在疫区资源有限地区部署标准化即时分子检测方法,是当务之急的公共卫生优先事项。医学实验室通过结合病毒载量数据与临床和暴露信息,为风险分层提供关键支撑。

papers.abstract_zh: 尼帕病毒 (NiV) 是一种后果严重的人畜共患 亨尼帕病毒,其特征是严重的 脑炎 和呼吸窘迫,导致 暴发 复发,在印度和孟加拉国,病死率在 40% 至 75% 之间。在这些 暴发 中,“超级传播”动态发挥着关键作用,其中一小部分个体导致了不成比例的大量继发感染。为了评估 尼帕病毒 感染中人类感染性和病毒载量动力学之间的关系,并确定医学实验室在识别潜在超级传播者方面的作用,通过在 PubMed、Scopus 和 ScienceDirect 上对 1998 年至 2025 年发表的同行评审文献进行系统搜索,进行了叙述性综述。定性综合表明,NiV 感染性高度依赖于样本基质效率和解剖脱落模式。在急性症状期,呼吸道标本产生最高的病毒 RNA 拷贝数,与活性飞沫 传播 密切相关。呼吸道样本中持续低于 25 (Ct < 25) 的实时 RT-PCR 循环阈值可作为高风险脱落者的间接实验室指标,应与临床和流行病学发现一起解释。然而,综合分析表明,超级传播本质上是多因素的。通过一线分子诊断进行早期识别仍然是打破 NiV 传播 链的基石。尽管独立的病毒载量阈值本身不足以预测传播事件,但医学实验室通过将纵向 Ct 动力学与临床和暴露数据相结合,提供了重要的风险概况。加强区域实验室基础设施并在流行、资源有限的地区部署标准化的即时分子检测是紧迫的公共卫生优先事项。

papers.title: Emerging infectious diseases (Mpox, Nipah, and Andes): A narrative review of transmission, environmental survival, and disinfection
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus are emerging infectious diseases that cause outbreaks associated with nosocomial transmission. METHODS: This narrative review summarizes the Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, and treatment with a focus on environmental survival, susceptibility to antiseptics and disinfectants, and infection prevention. RESULTS: Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus all survive in the environment and are capable of indirect transmission. All these viruses are enveloped and susceptible to commonly used antiseptics and surface disinfectants. CONCLUSIONS: Rapid identification of patients with known or suspected infections of these emerging viruses coupled with adherence to infection prevention recommendations will prevent healthcare-associated transmission.

papers.title: STRUCTURAL AND FUNCTIONAL INSIGHTS INTO THE REPLICASE/TRANSCRIPTASE SYSTEMS OF THE DEADLY BAT-BORNE HUMAN VIRUSES: MARBURG, EBOLA, AND NIPAH
papers.abstract: Replication and transcription of genomes in the human pathogenic viruses, viz. Marburg, Ebola and Nipah are accomplished by a virally encoded RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp). The enzyme performs this dual function with a polymerase cofactor, VP35, in Marburg and Ebola viruses and a phosphoprotein, P, in Nipah and its related viruses. As RdRp is indispensable for the viral lifecycle, it is one of the most attractive molecular targets for the development of broad-spectrum antiviral therapeutics to control the spread of these viruses. However, until now, little is known about the RdRp of these viruses, especially with respect to their active sites, polymerase catalytic centre and its catalytic mechanism, which are considered the most promising molecular targets for drug development initiatives. In this study, multiple sequence alignment (MSA) was integrated with structural information from X-ray crystallography, cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and site-directed mutagenesis (SDM) studies to identify the putative catalytic and metal-binding sites of the RdRp from Marburg, Ebola and Nipah viruses. MSA analysis suggests that the RdRp from these viruses uses an -LA/VG- as the template-binding pair, an invariant K, as the proton abstractor which initiates the catalysis and an invariant R at -4 from the catalytic K, as the nucleotide discriminator, all of which are highly or completely conserved. Besides, the Marburg and Ebola viruses contain an additional second putative polymerase catalytic core within the N-terminal domain (NTD), which is absent in the Nipah virus polymerase. The identified catalytic residues exhibit strong structural similarity to the conserved polymerase catalytic site architectures already reported in numerous RNA- and DNA-dependent polymerases, supporting a common catalytic framework. The catalytic magnesium-binding sites are also completely conserved among these viruses and consist of two invariant aspartate-containing motifs, -GDN- and -TDL-. This arrangement differs slightly from that what is reported for several other non-segmented negative-sense RNA viruses, including influenza, rabies, mumps and measles, which typically use -GDN- and -G/SDD- motifs for catalytic magnesium-binding. Furthermore, the RdRp domains of all three viruses contain two putative zinc-binding motifs (ZBMs), suggesting an important structural role in polymerase stability and function. Interestingly, the RdRp of Marburg and Ebola viruses, members of the Filoviridae family, possess an additional putative HNH-endonuclease motif(s) that is absent in the Nipah virus polymerase, a member of the Paramyxoviridae family. Collectively, these findings reveal conserved structural and catalytic features of the polymerases from these bat-borne human pathogens, and provide new insights into their evolutionary relationships, and also identify potential molecular targets for rational antiviral drug design.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate the structural and functional characteristics of the RdRp in Nipah virus and related bat-borne human viruses, as understanding these features is critical for developing antiviral therapeutics. The research was motivated by the lack of knowledge about the RdRp's active sites, catalytic centre and mechanism, which are key targets for drug development.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study focused on the Nipah virus and its related bat-borne human viruses, specifically Marburg, Ebola and Nipah viruses. It integrated multiple sequence alignment with structural data from X-ray crystallography, cryo-electron microscopy and site-directed mutagenesis to analyze the RdRp of these viruses.
analysis.methods: The study used multiple sequence alignment (MSA) combined with structural information from X-ray crystallography, cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and site-directed mutagenesis (SDM) to identify the catalytic and metal-binding sites of the RdRp from Nipah virus and related viruses. These methods were employed to compare the structural features of the RdRp across the studied viruses.
analysis.main_results: The MSA analysis revealed that the RdRp of Nipah virus and related viruses uses an -LA/VG- as the template-binding pair, an invariant K as the proton abstractor initiating catalysis, and an invariant R at -4 from the catalytic K as the nucleotide discriminator, all of which are highly or completely conserved. The catalytic magnesium-binding sites were also found to be completely conserved, consisting of two invariant aspartate-containing motifs, -GDN- and -TDL-.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that the RdRp of Nipah virus and related viruses shares structural and catalytic features with other RNA- and DNA-dependent polymerases, indicating a common catalytic framework. These results provide new insights into the evolutionary relationships among these viruses and highlight potential molecular targets for antiviral drug design.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The identification of conserved structural and catalytic features of the RdRp in Nipah virus and related viruses can inform the development of broad-spectrum antiviral therapeutics, which is crucial for controlling outbreaks and preventing the spread of these deadly pathogens.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its reliance on structural data from other viruses, which may not fully capture the unique characteristics of Nipah virus. However, the evidence is strong as it is based on multiple sequence alignment and structural analysis, supporting a common catalytic framework among the studied viruses.

analysis.summary_en: This study provides structural and functional insights into the RdRp of Nipah virus and related bat-borne human viruses, including Marburg and Ebola. The research aimed to address the lack of knowledge about the RdRp's active sites, catalytic centre and mechanism, which are critical for antiviral drug development. Using multiple sequence alignment and structural data from X-ray crystallography, cryo-electron microscopy, and site-directed mutagenesis, the study identified conserved features of the RdRp, including the template-binding pair, proton abstractor, and nucleotide discriminator. These findings suggest a common catalytic framework among these viruses and offer new perspectives on their evolutionary relationships. The results highlight potential molecular targets for rational antiviral drug design, which could have significant implications for controlling outbreaks. However, the study's reliance on structural data from other viruses may limit its specificity, and the evidence is considered strong due to the integration of multiple analytical methods.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨 尼帕病毒 及其相关蝙蝠源性人类病毒的 RdRp 的结构和功能特征,因为了解这些特征对于开发 抗病毒药物 治疗药物至关重要。研究的动机源于对 RdRp 活性位点、催化中心及其机制缺乏了解,而这些是药物开发的关键靶标。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究聚焦于 尼帕病毒 及其相关蝙蝠源性人类病毒,特别是马尔堡病毒、埃博拉病毒和 尼帕病毒。研究整合了多序列比对与来自 X 射线晶体学、冷冻电子显微镜和定点诱变的结构数据,以分析这些病毒的 RdRp。
elements_zh.methods: 本研究采用多序列比对(MSA)结合来自 X 射线晶体学、冷冻电子显微镜(cryo-EM)和定点诱变(SDM)研究的结构信息,以识别 尼帕病毒 及其相关病毒的 RdRp 的催化和金属结合位点。这些方法用于比较所研究病毒的 RdRp 结构特征。
elements_zh.main_results: MSA 分析表明,尼帕病毒 及其相关病毒的 RdRp 使用 -LA/VG- 作为模板结合对,一个不变的 K 作为质子抽取剂,启动催化反应,并且一个位于催化 K 前第 4 位的不变 R 作为核苷酸识别器,所有这些都高度或完全保守。此外,催化镁结合位点也被发现完全保守,由两个不变的天冬氨酸含有的模体 -GDN- 和 -TDL- 组成。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,尼帕病毒 及其相关病毒的 RdRp 在结构和催化方面与其它 RNA 和 DNA 依赖性聚合酶共享特征,表明存在一种共同的催化框架。这些结果为这些病毒之间的进化关系提供了新的见解,并突出了潜在的分子靶标,用于 抗病毒药物 药物设计。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 在 尼帕病毒 及其相关病毒中识别出 RdRp 的保守结构和催化特征,可以为开发广谱 抗病毒药物 治疗药物提供信息,这对于控制 暴发 并防止这些致命病原体的传播至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其依赖于其他病毒的结构数据,这可能无法完全捕捉 尼帕病毒 的独特特征。然而,证据是强有力的,因为它基于多序列比对和结构分析,支持了所研究病毒之间存在共同的催化框架。

papers.abstract_zh: 在人类致病病毒马尔堡病毒、埃博拉病毒和尼帕病毒中,基因组 的复制和转录由病毒编码的 RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶(RdRp)完成。该酶在马尔堡病毒和埃博拉病毒中与聚合酶辅因子 VP35 一起执行这种双重功能,在尼帕病毒及其相关病毒中则与磷酸蛋白 P 一起执行。由于 RdRp 对病毒生命周期至关重要,它是开发广谱 抗病毒药物 治疗药物以控制这些病毒传播的最有吸引力的分子靶标之一。然而,直到现在,人们对这些病毒的 RdRp 了解甚少,尤其是其活性位点、聚合酶催化中心及其催化机制,这些被认为是药物开发计划中最有前景的分子靶标。本研究整合了多序列比对(MSA)与来自 X 射线晶体学、冷冻电子显微镜(cryo-EM)和定点诱变(SDM)研究的结构信息,以识别马尔堡病毒、埃博拉病毒和 尼帕病毒 的 RdRp 的潜在催化和金属结合位点。MSA 分析表明,这些病毒的 RdRp 使用 -LA/VG- 作为模板结合对,一个不变的 K 作为质子抽取剂,启动催化反应,并且一个位于催化 K 前第 4 位的不变 R 作为核苷酸识别器,所有这些都高度或完全保守。此外,马尔堡病毒和埃博拉病毒在其 N 端结构域(NTD)中包含一个额外的潜在聚合酶催化核心,而 尼帕病毒 聚合酶则没有。所鉴定的催化残基在结构上与已报道的许多 RNA 和 DNA 依赖性聚合酶的保守催化位点架构高度相似,支持了一种共同的催化框架。催化镁结合位点在这些病毒中也完全保守,由两个不变的天冬氨酸含有的模体 -GDN- 和 -TDL- 组成。这种排列与其他一些非分节负链 RNA 病毒(如流感病毒、狂犬病毒、腮腺炎病毒和麻疹病毒)略有不同,这些病毒通常使用 -GDN- 和 -G/SDD- 模体进行催化镁结合。此外,所有三种病毒的 RdRp 域包含两个潜在的锌结合模体(ZBMs),这表明它们在聚合酶稳定性和功能中具有重要的结构作用。有趣的是,马尔堡病毒和埃博拉病毒的 RdRp,作为丝状病毒科的成员,还包含一个额外的潜在 HNH 核酸内切酶模体,而 尼帕病毒 聚合酶,作为副粘病毒科的成员,则没有该模体。总体而言,这些发现揭示了这些蝙蝠源性人类病原体的聚合酶在结构和催化方面的保守特征,并提供了关于它们进化关系的新见解,同时识别了潜在的分子靶标,用于理性设计 抗病毒药物 药物。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 本研究旨在探讨 尼帕病毒 及其相关蝙蝠源性人类病毒的 RdRp 的结构和功能特征,因为了解这些特征对于开发 抗病毒药物 治疗药物至关重要。研究的动机源于对 RdRp 活性位点、催化中心及其机制缺乏了解,而这些是药物开发的关键靶标。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 本研究聚焦于 尼帕病毒 及其相关蝙蝠源性人类病毒,特别是马尔堡病毒、埃博拉病毒和 尼帕病毒。研究整合了多序列比对与来自 X 射线晶体学、冷冻电子显微镜和定点诱变的结构数据,以分析这些病毒的 RdRp。
analysis_zh.methods: 本研究采用多序列比对(MSA)结合来自 X 射线晶体学、冷冻电子显微镜(cryo-EM)和定点诱变(SDM)研究的结构信息,以识别 尼帕病毒 及其相关病毒的 RdRp 的催化和金属结合位点。这些方法用于比较所研究病毒的 RdRp 结构特征。
analysis_zh.main_results: MSA 分析表明,尼帕病毒 及其相关病毒的 RdRp 使用 -LA/VG- 作为模板结合对,一个不变的 K 作为质子抽取剂,启动催化反应,并且一个位于催化 K 前第 4 位的不变 R 作为核苷酸识别器,所有这些都高度或完全保守。此外,催化镁结合位点也被发现完全保守,由两个不变的天冬氨酸含有的模体 -GDN- 和 -TDL- 组成。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现表明,尼帕病毒 及其相关病毒的 RdRp 在结构和催化方面与其它 RNA 和 DNA 依赖性聚合酶共享特征,表明存在一种共同的催化框架。这些结果为这些病毒之间的进化关系提供了新的见解,并突出了潜在的分子靶标,用于 抗病毒药物 药物设计。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 在 尼帕病毒 及其相关病毒中识别出 RdRp 的保守结构和催化特征,可以为开发广谱 抗病毒药物 治疗药物提供信息,这对于控制 暴发 并防止这些致命病原体的传播至关重要。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 本研究的局限性在于其依赖于其他病毒的结构数据,这可能无法完全捕捉 尼帕病毒 的独特特征。然而,证据是强有力的,因为它基于多序列比对和结构分析,支持了所研究病毒之间存在共同的催化框架。
